Alex / Vanessa — quick technical note from the runtime/ops perspective to help your engineers decide. High-level recommendations follow; happy to expand in the tech sync.

Embedding dimensionality
- 768: smallest index footprint, lower latency for vector distance; expect some accuracy loss for mixed title+desc queries.
- 1024: reasonable baseline, close to Vecly. If your recall is already good, migrating to 1024 keeps reindex cost low.
- 1536: typically yields incremental improvements (often ~2–5% in recall@10 depending on data). The biggest drawback is index size (~1.5x vs 1024) and RAM/cold-start reindex time.

Normalization and scoring
- Keep L2 unit normalization for cosine-similarity scoring; this gives consistent nearest-neighbor behavior across models. We do not recommend per-vector scaling unless you have a domain-specific signal to compress (e.g., popularity score baked into vector).

Batching & throughput
- For inference (embedding generation): aim for request batching of 8–32 for throughput on GPU-backed Redwood Dedicated. For CPU/hosted, use smaller batches (1–8).
- For nearest-neighbor scoring during migration evaluation (side-by-side scoring): run async scoring in background jobs to avoid tail latency on critical search paths. We can stream top-K candidates from Redwood then re-rank locally if you prefer.

Migration patterns
- Dual-write + offline evaluation: easiest for parity checks. Write to both Vecly and Redwood during a sampling window, collect scores, and compute metrics offline on the 5k test set you agreed on.
- Parallel scoring (no dual-ingest): send a copy of each query to Redwood for scoring only (no index writes) and compare results client-side. This avoids duplicate ingestion into your ANN index.
- Canary reindex: do an offline reindex to Redwood-backed index for a subset of partitions (if your search infra supports sharding); route 5–10% of traffic to those partitions.

Auth & routing
- We support API keys and JWT-based service accounts. For per-route routing, two options:
  1) Client-side/proxy routing: your proxy maps route -> API key (recommended initially).
  2) Redwood routing rules: we can provision model aliases and an ingress rule to send a percentage of traffic to a model variant. This requires a small config change on our side (we can help).

Attachments: auth-routing-snippet.txt (example of per-route header mapping)

Actionable suggestion for the sync:
- Tech sync agenda: (1) confirm metric set and test vectors, (2) decide migration pattern (dual-write vs parallel scoring), (3) auth/routing approach, (4) perf expectations and quantization options for cost control.

If this looks good I can join the sync and walk through the auth-snippet and a short demo of parallel scoring.

Alex / Samir — thanks for the quick replies and the good questions. Based on Kim's notes below and your constraints around reindex time, here's a proposed path and owners so we can lock the tech sync (Tue 2026-11-24 10:30am PST tentative):

Decisions (proposed)
- Dimensionality: start at 1024 to minimize reindex overhead; evaluate a 1536 variant only if recall@10 on the 5k eval set is meaningfully higher (>3%).
- Normalization: keep unit L2 normalization (no per-vector scaling).
- Migration: do parallel scoring (no dual-ingest) for two weeks to compare real traffic results, then do a canary reindex if metrics look good.
- Auth/routing: use a proxy-based per-route API key mapping initially; Redwood will provision a model alias and provide a fallback variant we can switch to via config.

Action items
- BrightCart (Alex / Samir): share the 5k sample vectors and evaluation script by EOD Friday (2026-11-26).
- Redwood (Vanessa/Kim): provide a small test harness to accept queries for parallel scoring and a sample auth-routing snippet (attached).
- Scheduling: confirm Tue 11/24 10:30am PST or propose alternate window.

If this plan works, we'll follow up with a short Miro doc capturing the eval matrix and responsibilities. Thank you — excited to move this forward.
